title: FeatureSpec
description: Structured spec of RUNLTS register-value-aware predictor component (sR), distilled from paper text.

source.paper_title: RUNLTS: Register-value-aware Predictor Utilizing Nested Large Tables
source.citation: Toru Koizumi, Toshiki Maekawa, Masanari Mizuno, Maru Kuroki, Tomoaki Tsumura, and Ryota Shioya. 2025. RUNLTS: Register-value-aware Predictor Utilizing Nested Large Tables. In Proceedings of the 6th Championship Branch Prediction (CBP 2025), in conjunction with ISCA 2025, June 21, 2025, Tokyo, Japan, pp. 1-6.

summary: sR is a register-value-aware neural statistical corrector (SC) component that captures correlations between branch directions and recently generated register values. It tracks available register values using a Tomasulo-like status table, compresses each 64-bit register value into a 12-bit digest (using format-specific XOR folding, exponent extraction, or bit replication), and groups 65 logical registers into 8 stride-8 banks. For each bank, usefulness tables select the most useful available register digest to index three prediction weight tables. Useful contributions are scaled by 2.5 and summed across banks into sR, which feeds into the overall SC summation (LSUM). Stale digests are invalidated after 256 decoded instructions. In RUNLTS, sR provides the single largest and broadest MPKI reduction across all benchmark categories.

state.name: prediction_weight_tables
state.organization: 8 banks, each containing 3 tables: WT0 (512 entries), WT1 (256 entries), WT2 (128 entries); total 7168 entries across all banks
state.indexing: h0, h1, h2 = hash_k(PC, selected_reg_digest). For WT0, 9-bit index (PC ^ (digest << 1) ^ (digest >> 3) & 0x1FF). For WT1, 8-bit index (& 0xFF). For WT2, 7-bit index (& 0x7F).

state.name: usefulness_weight_tables
state.organization: 8 banks, each containing 3 tables: UT0 (8 entries), UT1 (8 entries), UT2 (8 entries). Each entry stores a usefulness weight for every logical register in the bank (bank 0 has 9 registers R0, R8, ..., R64; banks 1-7 have 8 registers each; total 65 registers)
state.entry_format: 6-bit signed usefulness counter per register in bank (bank 0: 9 x 6 bits = 54 bits/entry; banks 1-7: 8 x 6 bits = 48 bits/entry)
state.indexing: 3-bit index per table (8 entries) indexed by skewed PC hash functions: idx0 = PC[5:3] ^ PC[8:6], idx1 = (PC >> 4) ^ (PC >> 7) & 0x7, idx2 = (PC >> 6) ^ (PC >> 9) & 0x7.

state.name: register_status_table
state.organization: Direct-mapped table with 65 entries corresponding to logical registers 0 to 64
state.entry_format: valid (1 bit), payload (14 bits: stores 14-bit ROB index when valid=0, or 12-bit digest when valid=1), decay_ctr (8 bits: counts decoded instructions up to 256)
state.indexing: Direct-mapped by logical register index r (0 <= r < 65)

algorithms.name: generate_digest
algorithms.trigger: lookup time / execution completion: when an instruction finishes execution and produces a result value
algorithms.notes: For INT, count_trailing/leading counts consecutive identical bits starting from LSB/MSB, capped at 63. Digest is exactly 12 bits.

algorithms.name: predict
algorithms.trigger: lookup time: during SC computation when predicting a branch at PC
algorithms.notes: If no register in the bank is valid, the bank contributes 0. Multiplier x0 vs x2.5 is determined by the bank's max usefulness.

algorithms.name: update
algorithms.trigger: commit time: when a branch resolves and the SC update conditions are met (|LSUM| <= theta or mispredicted)
algorithms.notes: Only registers available at prediction time are updated. Randomly picking one available register per bank preserves single-write-port RAM implementation. Weights saturate at [-32, 31].

algorithms.name: instruction_decode
algorithms.trigger: lookup time / decode stage: on each decoded instruction (with destination register rd, if any)
algorithms.notes: Invalidates previous digest as a new definition is now in flight.

algorithms.name: instruction_complete
algorithms.trigger: lookup time / execution stage: when an instruction completing execution writes value to register rd
algorithms.pseudocode:
function generate_digest(reg_type, val_64bit):
  if reg_type == 0: // INT
    trail = count_trailing_zeros(val_64bit) & 0x3F
    lead = count_leading_zeros(val_64bit) & 0x3F
    lsb = val_64bit & 0x3F
    return (trail & 0x3F) ^ ((lead & 0x3F) << 3) ^ ((lsb & 0x3F) << 6)
  else if reg_type == 1: // FP64
    return ((val_64bit >> 55) & 0x1FF) << 3
  else if reg_type == 2: // FP32
    return ((val_64bit >> 26) & 0x3F) << 3
  else if reg_type == 3: // FP16
    return ((val_64bit >> 13) & 0x7) << 3
  else if reg_type == 4: // FLAGS
    flags = val_64bit & 0xF
    return flags | (flags << 4) | (flags << 8)
  return 0

function on_complete(rd, rob_index, val_64bit, reg_type):
  if rd >= 0 and rd < 65:
    if register_status_table[rd].valid == 0 and register_status_table[rd].payload == (rob_index & 0x3FFF):
      digest = generate_digest(reg_type, val_64bit)
      register_status_table[rd].payload = digest
      register_status_table[rd].valid = 1
      register_status_table[rd].decay_ctr = 0
algorithms.notes: Updates payload with 12-bit digest and asserts valid bit.

algorithms.name: decay_step
algorithms.trigger: lookup time / decode stage: called once per decoded instruction
algorithms.notes: Ensures stale digests (>256 decoded instructions old) do not contaminate predictions.

algorithms.name: mispredict_recovery
algorithms.trigger: squash: on a branch misprediction flush
algorithms.notes: As observed in Section 4.2, instructions finished before the flush retain their digests, supplying fresh register values immediately to following branches.

host_interfaces.need: register values and completion notification at execution unit
host_interfaces.description: 64-bit produced value, register type (INT, FP, FLAG), logical destination register index, and ROB tag from execution unit upon instruction completion
host_interfaces.fallback: If execution units cannot provide values early, forward digests only at retirement/commit (losing early post-mispredict value correlation).

host_interfaces.need: destination register and ROB index at decode/rename
host_interfaces.description: Logical destination register ID and assigned ROB index for every decoded instruction that writes a register
host_interfaces.fallback: Track register readiness at dispatch/issue stage instead of decode.

host_interfaces.description: Tick notification indicating instruction decode progression to advance the 256-instruction decay counters
host_interfaces.fallback: Tick decay counter per predicted branch or cycle scaled by average IPC.

host_interfaces.description: Signal and ROB range of flushed instructions when a branch mispredicts
host_interfaces.fallback: Invalidate all in-flight (valid=0) entries in the register status table unconditionally on any squash.

resource_accounting.storage_breakdown: Prediction weight tables (WT): 6 bits * (128 + 256 + 512) entries * 8 banks = 43,008 bits. Usefulness weight tables (UT): 6 bits * 65 registers * (8 + 8 + 8) entries = 9,360 bits. Register tracking table: 65 registers * (1 valid + 14 payload + 8 decay) = 1,495 bits. Total = 43,008 + 9,360 + 1,495 = 53,863 bits (6.57 KiB).
resource_accounting.logic_cost_notes: Requires 12-bit digest generation logic (leading/trailing zero count, XOR gates), 8-bank parallel usefulness argmax comparisons, and 2.5x fixed-point multiplier per bank.
resource_accounting.budget_donors: To maintain iso-storage under a fixed budget, reduce high-bank tagged table entries in TAGE (e.g., evicting ~2 banks saves 69,632 bits) or reduce Bimodal entries from 128K to 64K (saves 81,920 bits).

parameters.name: num_banks
parameters.storage_impact: Scales prediction weight table storage linearly with bank count

parameters.name: num_registers
parameters.storage_impact: Scales UT size (6 bits * num_registers * 24) and register_status_table size (23 bits * num_registers)

parameters.name: wt0_entries
parameters.storage_impact: Increases WT storage by 6 bits * wt0_entries * num_banks

parameters.name: wt1_entries
parameters.storage_impact: Increases WT storage by 6 bits * wt1_entries * num_banks

parameters.name: wt2_entries
parameters.storage_impact: Increases WT storage by 6 bits * wt2_entries * num_banks

parameters.name: ut_entries_per_table
parameters.storage_impact: Increases UT storage by 6 bits * num_registers * 3 tables * ut_entries_per_table

parameters.name: weight_bits
parameters.storage_impact: Scales all WT and UT weights proportionally

parameters.name: decay_threshold
parameters.storage_impact: log2(decay_threshold) determines width of decay counter in register_status_table

parameters.name: digest_bits
parameters.storage_impact: Affects payload width in register_status_table if > 14 bits

unit_tests.name: test_int_digest_generation
unit_tests.given: 64-bit integer value 0x0000_0000_0000_0040 (trailing zeros = 6, leading zeros = 57, LSBs [5:0] = 0x00)

unit_tests.name: test_stale_digest_decay
unit_tests.given: Register R4 completes with a valid digest at tick 0. Exactly 256 instruction decode ticks occur with no new writes to R4.
unit_tests.expect: register_status_table[4].valid transitions from 1 to 0 on the 256th tick

unit_tests.name: test_most_useful_selection
unit_tests.given: Bank 0 has two valid registers: R0 with cumulative usefulness (UT0+UT1+UT2) = 15, and R8 with cumulative usefulness = 28.
unit_tests.expect: Bank 0 selects R8 digest to index WT0, WT1, WT2, and scales bank 0 output by 2.5 since max_useful (28) > 0

unit_tests.name: test_training_single_port_random_selection
unit_tests.given: Branch commits where Bank 1 had both R1 and R9 valid at prediction time.
unit_tests.expect: Exactly one of R1 or R9 is pseudo-randomly selected for weight and usefulness updates; only 1 write port is accessed per table

open_questions: The paper does not state the exact tie-breaking rule when multiple available registers in a bank share the same maximum usefulness; assumed lowest register ID wins.
The paper does not define the exact counting rule for leading/trailing zeros/ones (e.g. saturation at 63 vs modulo 64); assumed saturated at 63.
The paper does not detail the hardware classifier distinguishing FP16, FP32, and FP64 from 64-bit raw register payloads; assumed ISA-provided register file type or instruction opcode hint.
The wire driving the per-bank x0 vs x2.5 multiplier in Figure 5(c) is unlabelled; assumed driven by (max_useful > 0) of the selected register in that bank.
